high.title: USD and Oil Prices Surge Due to Middle East Conflict: How Will Exchange Rates and Inflation in Vietnam Be Affected?
high.summary: The escalation of Middle East tensions following US-Israeli strikes on Iran has immediately impacted global commodity markets, with oil prices surging due to supply disruption fears. The USD Index (DXY) jumped 0.8% to 98.42 points, while global gold prices also rose, reflecting clear "risk-off" sentiment in financial markets. For Vietnam, Vietcombank Securities (VCBS) warns that increased geopolitical uncertainty could trigger capital flow reallocation toward safe-haven assets. This creates upward pressure on USD/VND exchange rates and potential inflationary pressures through higher import costs, particularly energy. The situation threatens to derail central banks' rate-cutting plans globally, with some potentially raising rates to combat oil-driven inflation. Vietnamese policymakers must monitor these developments closely as they could impact monetary policy decisions and FX stability.

high.title: USD Price Hits Ceiling, Free Market Exceeds 27,000 VND/USD
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam set the central exchange rate at 25,059 VND/USD, up 2 VND from the previous week. Commercial banks have quoted USD at the ceiling rate for selling, with significant increases in buying rates. Vietcombank quotes 26,041-26,311 VND/USD (buy-sell), up 40 VND on the buying side and 2 VND on selling. VietinBank increased buying rates by 57 VND to 26,089-26,311 VND/USD. The free market saw USD trading at 26,850-26,880 VND/USD, breaking the psychological 27,000 level. This reflects global USD strength amid heightened geopolitical risks from Middle East tensions. The pressure on VND comes as oil prices surge 8-13% in just days, creating inflationary pressures globally and making central banks more cautious about rate cuts. This USD strength threatens to import inflation into Vietnam and could force SBV intervention to maintain exchange rate stability.

high.title: Middle East Tensions Impact USD Pricing
high.summary: SBV Deputy Governor Pham Thanh Ha highlighted that Middle East tensions have driven oil prices up 8-13% in just days, creating additional global inflationary pressure. This environment makes many major central banks more cautious about interest rate cuts, with some signaling potential rate increases instead. In Vietnam, USD exchange rates show upward pressure with the central rate at 25,057 VND/USD, up 13 VND over one week. Commercial banks quote around 26,029-26,309 VND/USD while free market rates hit 26,850-26,880 VND/USD. The developments reflect global USD strength amid geopolitical risk escalation. For Vietnamese monetary policy, this creates a challenging environment where external inflationary pressures through higher oil prices and stronger USD could limit SBV's policy flexibility, potentially forcing more hawkish stances to maintain price stability and exchange rate balance.

medium.title: VN-Index Lost Over 113 Points in 1 Week, Experts Identify "Oversold" Stock Groups
medium.summary: VN-Index closed the first week of March down 113 points to 1,767 points, similar to the "tariff shock" in April 2025. The decline was driven by escalating Middle East geopolitical tensions, creating intense investor anxiety. Foreign investors continued net selling over 6,000 billion VND despite Vietnam's potential FTSE Russell upgrade review approaching.

medium.title: BIDV Interest Rates March 2025: Which Terms Have the Highest Rates?
medium.summary: BIDV maintains stable deposit rates in March 2026 with demand deposits at 0.1%/year. Short-term 1-2 month deposits earn 2.1%/year, while 3-month and 5-month terms offer 2.4%/year. The highest rates of 5.3%/year apply to long-term deposits from 24-36 months, providing attractive options for long-term savers.

medium.title: Military Bank Just Increased Savings Interest Rates Strongly
medium.summary: MB significantly raised deposit rates for terms over 12 months while keeping shorter terms unchanged. For deposits under 1 billion VND, 12-18 month rates increased from 5.5% to 6.1% annually, while 24-60 month terms rose from 6.3% to 6.6%. This reflects competitive pressure in the deposit market as banks seek to attract funding.

medium.title: Over 1.2 Trillion VND on Vietnam Stock Market Held by Foreign Investors: Awaiting Upgrade Turning Point
medium.summary: Despite years of net selling totaling 260,000 billion VND, foreign investors still hold over 1.2 trillion VND in market capitalization (12% of total market). About 30% of global emerging market funds have invested in Vietnam, with nearly 40% of Asian investment funds holding Vietnamese stocks, showing continued structural interest despite recent selling pressure.

medium.title: Experts: Securities Market Next Week May Fall to 1,700 Points Level
medium.summary: Vietnam's stock market suffered its first week of March amid global financial volatility from escalating Middle East tensions. VN-Index fell 112.49 points (-5.98%) to 1,767.84 points with liquidity 50% above 20-week average. Analysts note continued foreign net selling pressure of over 6,000 billion VND despite approaching FTSE Russell upgrade consideration.

medium.title: Record Historic Stock Market Drop Triggers Surprising Series of Forecasts
medium.summary: VN-Index lost 115 points (-6.51%) in a historic sell-off, with VNDirect identifying key support levels at 1,660-1,600-1,500 points. Valuation below 1,660 points becomes attractive as P/E forward falls below 5-year average while P/B approaches levels where long-term funds typically accumulate during correction cycles.
